ca_cool_dome.blurb: Cool Dome is a small formation in the Wonderland of Rocks at the north end of Joshua Tree National Park, with eleven routes, mostly trad plus a few bolted lines. Grades cluster around 5.9 and 5.10, with a handful of easier climbs and one 5.11. The rock is granodiorite with desert varnish on the east side. Its character depends on which face you pick: the south and west sides take sun all day, which helps on a chilly day, while the east side stays shaded and suits hot weather. Expect a quiet outing, since the walk in from the north-side trails is a long one.

ca_ginger_s_face.blurb: Ginger's Face is one of three crags on the rocky hillside called Gilligan's Island, at the entrance to Wonderland North in Joshua Tree National Park. It has eleven routes, mostly traditional leads with a few top-rope lines, running from about 5.7 up to 5.10, with four of them in the 5.10 range. The hillside gets shade in the morning and sun in the afternoon, and the climbing is mostly moderate cracks and faces with decent gear. Reaching it means a flat hike followed by a short scramble up the hillside, so expect roughly half an hour or more from the car.

ca_coyote_ridge_boulder.blurb: Coyote Ridge Boulder sits among rocky outcrops on the ridge above Tennessee Valley in the Marin Headlands, with views over the Marin coast. The one overhanging boulder holds eleven problems that run from easy V0 up through V8, with a good number of mid-grade V5 and harder lines, so it leans toward strong boulderers. Rock quality is uneven and generally sharp, so expect rough skin. The walk from the roadhead is short, about ten to fifteen minutes, along a trail that can get overgrown with poison oak in spring.

ca_zodiac_boulder.blurb: Zodiac Boulder is the first block you meet when arriving at the main Purple Stones North area, in a creek canyon of the Santa Monica Mountains just off Topanga Canyon Boulevard. A rusted car axle on its north side helps identify it. It has eleven problems from very easy up to V6, with a cluster at V1 and V4, and the best lines tend to be on the left side. The climbing is described as bold, so bring plenty of pads and spotters. The rock can turn soft and brittle after rain, so let it dry for a few days.

ca_h_west_face.blurb: The West Face is a sunny, southwest-facing wall of Fresno Dome, a granodiorite dome in the Sierra foothills above Oakhurst at about 7,100 feet. It has eleven routes, roughly two-thirds bolted and the rest trad, all between 5.9 and 5.11. Most are multi-pitch, running two to four pitches, so it suits climbers comfortable on longer routes and sustained 5.10 and 5.11 terrain. The rock is high quality and the surrounding dome area sees few crowds. The grade spread is tilted hard: only one route sits at 5.9, with the remainder split between 5.10 and 5.11.

ca_mt_goode.blurb: Mt. Goode is a 13,085-foot peak on the Sierra crest above the South Fork of Bishop Creek, reached from the South Lake trailhead via the Bishop Pass trail. Its north face is the draw, with a striking buttress and a mix of trad and alpine lines. Eleven climbs run from an easy scramble and fourth-class ridges, through 5.9 and 5.10 multi-pitch routes, up to a few 5.11s and one 5.13. The main routes need around 4.5 miles and 2,500 feet of gain to reach the base, yet they can be done car to car in a single day. Most routes face north, so expect shade and cold.
